passage.text: Spotify is a Swedish music streaming company that grew very fast and changed the music industry. Its people say they want to make mistakes faster than anyone else. To keep the spirit of a small start-up, Spotify organises work in small self-steering teams. These teams decide how to do their jobs and write their experiments on whiteboards. They measure what happens, keep the ideas that work and drop the ones that do not. Some teams have a "Fail Wall", and internal blogs share both successes and failures. The HR director explains that the company values innovation more than predictability, because you cannot predict the future.

source.title: Corporate Rebels: Make Work More Fun, Chapter 4, pp. 104–106

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Spotify stays innovative by encouraging teams to experiment, measure results, and learn from failures quickly.
wrong: Spotify values predictability and careful planning more than taking risks.
Spotify's success comes from having large, centralized management teams.
taps.explain: The excerpt emphasizes speed, experimentation, and learning from failure.

taps.context: To keep the spirit of a small start-up, Spotify organises work in small self-steering teams.
taps.correct: Spotify uses small independent teams to maintain the flexible culture of a young company.
wrong: Spotify became large by copying the structure of start-ups.
Spotify's small teams prevent the company from growing like a start-up.
taps.explain: The original sentence explains Spotify's purpose for team structure; the paraphrase says the same thing simply.
